title: Wrong answer? Say why, not just incorrect

media.alt: K&A Performance slide on a whiteboard: Feedback that teaches. Wrong answer? Say why, not just “incorrect.” The word Incorrect. is struck through in red marker. Below it, magnets hold a real screen from our nutrition sample course: On your counter, Brown rice, and its feedback, Try another part of the plate. Brown rice is a whole grain. It retains its bran and germ. Marker note: Say what to try, and why. 5 rules, each shown on a real wrong answer in one of our sample courses.

Rule 1 of 5 on the whiteboard: Name what went wrong. Not just that it is wrong, but which part. Then the learner fixes the right thing. Real screen from The RFI that gets answered: four fields filled, with References holding This is the third time the drawings have contradicted themselves, and Proposal holding Also, please confirm the paint color in the lobby, both outlined in red. The feedback reads: Needs another pass: References, Proposal. Match each field to its job. Complaints and unrelated questions stay out of this request. Marker note: It names the two fields that need another pass.

Rule 2 of 5 on the whiteboard: Point at the rule. Send them back to the idea that decides the answer, so the next try comes from the rule, not a guess. Real screen from Strong is a skill: the task card Rising from a low chair, placed in Hinge, and the feedback Try a different station. Notice whether the task lowers and rises, moves mainly at the hips, pushes, pulls or travels with a load. Marker note: It points at the five movement patterns.

Rule 3 of 5 on the whiteboard: Show the right move. When the method is the lesson, show the working, so they can see where their number went off. Real screen from The P&L, read like an owner: Price the five-point change. Baseline revenue stays $80,000. COGS rises from 40% to 45%. Enter the new operating income. The answer 5000 is entered, and the feedback reads: Recheck the figures. $80,000 less $36,000 COGS less $43,000 operating expenses leaves $1,000. Marker note: It shows the working, step by step.

Rule 4 of 5 on the whiteboard: Let them retry. Mark the miss, leave it open, and ask for another go. The full explanation comes once they get it. Real screen from Spot it before it hurts someone: the situation Open second-floor edge, where crews cross all day for the next three months, with Add task-matched protective equipment placed, a Remove placement link, and the note Review this placement: Revisit this placement. Read the situation and try a different control. Marker note: The control can be moved. Try a different one.

Rule 5 of 5 on the whiteboard: Keep it short. What to try, then why, in a line or two. Then get out of the way. Real screen from Build the plate, skip the diet: Brown rice on your counter, the plate with its vegetables and fruit half and its protein and grains quarters, and the feedback Try another part of the plate. Brown rice is a whole grain. It retains its bran and germ. Marker note: Brown rice on the protein quarter: three short sentences.

Whiteboard recap: Wrong answer? Say why. 1 Name what went wrong. 2 Point at the rule. 3 Show the right move. 4 Let them retry. 5 Keep it short.
